dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: ...Did that all get a little heavy for you? I think you prefer me when I'm just teasing you, don't you? Hehe...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: That puppet was built with technology that has been lost to time. Perhaps she, as a god, is the only one privy to the knowledge of its origins...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Still... there is one other thing on this topic that I suspect you may be curious to know.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Before Ei began modifying her own godly form, she took it upon herself to create a prototype puppet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... you mean there are three Raiden Shoguns!?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: No, the prototype was merely a proof of concept. Its appearance and intellect were not based on Ei. It was a test.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The original plan was for Ei to simply discard it. But perhaps Ei thought this to be too cruel, because in the end she chose only to seal the power within it.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Later, this puppet wandered Inazuma as an ordinary human male with his own consciousness, until... the Fatui took an interest in him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, not the Fatui!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Some eccentric geniuses in the ranks of the Fatui made adjustments to the prototype, not only unsealing his power, but very likely rendering him even more formidable than his original specifications.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Surely you don't mean...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Mm-hmm. The object of divine creation is the one who has now taken possession of the Gnosis... and the prototype puppet is now known as "The Balladeer."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What in the... What a crazy story!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: It is, isn't it? Who can say whether it's coincidence or destiny.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I'm surprised an outlander like you is aware that there was once a change of Electro Archon... Few citizens of Inazuma are aware of this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Morax told us. He said that the Electro Archon, Baal, has passed away...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Yes. The truth of the matter is that there were two twin gods, Baal and Beelzebul.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Twin gods?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: They won the Archon War together, and when Baal established the Shogunate, Beelzebul became her Kagemusha, or "shadow warrior." In other words, she acted as Baal's body double.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Beelzebul is Ei, with whom we are now both acquainted. Baal's name was "Makoto."

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: As far as the world was aware, there were not two, but one. They complemented each other, and they ruled Inazuma jointly. So there was no need for the public to know the truth.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: In fact, the name "Baal" and the title of Raiden Shogun was understood to refer to both of them, right up until—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Until what?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Makoto died several hundred years ago in a war that I was not personally involved in. Since then, Ei has assumed the Shogunate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Losing her sister must have been super hard on Ei...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: That was when Ei began to change. Makoto was her greatest loss.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon feels like she understands Ei a lot better now after finding that out... So, what kind of god was Makoto?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I didn't spend a great deal of time with her, but my impression was... she was a gentle god, who in each moment cherished the beauty of what was before her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Sorry, I haven't a clue. I am also unfamiliar with the god you describe.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: But if you still have doubts about Ei, I would say they are misplaced.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Not only does she not fit your description, but she voluntarily gave up her Gnosis long ago, severing her ties with Celestia in the process.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Having met her, I don't believe she was the one.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: That's good to hear. Otherwise, given that I am her familiar, it could have made our relationship rather awkward, don't you think?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, we aren't looking to pick a fight with you!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehehe... I wish you the best of luck. May you soon discover the truth behind it all.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: #As for your {M#sister}{F#brother}'s whereabouts, I will use all the resources at my disposal to investigate it, and I will also borrow some of Ayato's people from the Shuumatsuban.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I'll let you know if I find out anything. Consider it part of my means of thanking you.

choices.text: About the next stop on my journey...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: After leaving Inazuma, hmm... I think it would be easiest for you to go to Sumeru.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, ooh, Sumeru! We've run into loads of scholars from there on our journey so far.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Yes, well, Sumeru is the land of the God of Wisdom, where the quest for wisdom and knowledge is never-ending.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: But their obsession gives rise to some truly inexplicable things. For example...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: In Sumeru, knowledge is holistically managed as a resource.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Knowledge... is a resource?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Yes. I don't know whether it was the sages or Lesser Lord Kusanali who came up with the idea.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lesser Lord Kusanali? That's a cute name.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh, you haven't heard? "Lesser Lord Kusanali" is the deity in whom the people of Sumeru place their faith. It's their chosen term of endearment for her.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I'm sure you must have some things to discuss with her, too. I wish you all the best.

choices.text: About the next stop on my journey...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Are you sure? Okay then. Oh, Traveler, do you still have the omamori I gave you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Of course. I'll keep it in a safe place.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Keep it safe? Is that all you intend to do with it?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: There was me thinking that you might hang it around your neck to show off to the world, telling everyone who inquired that it was given to you by none other than Yae Miko, the wise and beautiful.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who in their right mind would do that!?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehehe... Okay, I'll stop. Now, a question for you. Traveler, what is your ambition?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #To be reunited with my {F#brother}{M#sister}, I guess?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I see... But that is merely a small goal, based on what preoccupies you here and now.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Your ambition should be something that transcends the world below and the starry sky above. Something that shines in unison with fate itself.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Perhaps the reason you do not possess a Vision is that such an ambition has yet to be engendered within you... It's a possibility.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Continue on your journey and maybe that moment will come to pass.

choices.text: About the next stop on my journey...
About the next stop on my journey...
About the next stop on my journey...

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Have you heard? Armand's been doing much better recently. He still gets nervous when there are too many people, but he can at least express what he means.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Well, he'd better be! How will he become a comedian if he stutters in front of people?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: The staff member at Lepaute Horlogerie. You haven't seen him?

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: He's from the same village as us, and he wants to act in comedies. Unfortunately, he has a terrible stutter.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: They say that it's a long-term effect of him having fallen from the audience seats and hitting his head at a comedy show.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: I really liked that comedy too. I recall that it was called "Judgment," but nowadays, I feel like I can't really enjoy it.

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: I mean, the kid who wanted to become a comic actor was judged during a comedy called "Judgment"... and his sentence was to never become one.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: Poor Armand. What sin did he commit, and who was his judge?

dialogues.speaker: Arbon
dialogues.text: Have you seen the evaluation board? Seems like someone likes those clockwork penguins.

dialogues.speaker: Alberre
dialogues.text: I saw it. It's the one that talks about wanting to get to know Freminet, right? Sounds like someone who would like to strike up some further collaboration, if you ask me.

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Oh, we're talking about those clockwork penguins on that table. A diver named Freminet made them, and he then placed them in our store as a consignment.

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: He's a good lad with a pretty face. Soft-spoken fellow, but he's very good at making toys.

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: He seems a little melancholy, though. Like someone who lacks something that should've belonged to him...

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: I know that look, y'know — it's the same one that Arbon makes when he looks at his empty wallet. Don't suppose Freminet's in need of Mora, do you?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Don't be ridiculous. He didn't even discuss the profit-split when he came to talk about the consignment. He wasn't in it for the Mora.

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: True. But what else would trouble a lad of his age?

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Yeah, and he's a winsome fellow, too. I haven't seen the boss ever approve of a consignment.

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: He not only offered to set up an outdoor stall for the penguins, but even proposed a fifty-fifty split on the earnings.

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: Unfortunately, one could only call the sales middling. Many people came to look, sure, but there weren't many buyers.

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: That toy is very intricately designed, but I'd say that also makes it harder to play with... and harder to fix.

response.speaker: Arbon
response.text: Really, I didn't expect that anyone would leave a message about it on the board. Maybe there's a big client behind it, eh?

response.speaker: Alberre
response.text: Either way, we should tell the boss about it. Won't do to miss out on a good deal, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: I'll inform you if my efforts at the Northland Bank bear any fruit.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Arbon and Alberre don't seem to be in today.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: They took leave, said they had a new idea for toys. Weird, if you ask me.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: They usually can't think of anything but their favorite comedies — forget having any thoughts about toys.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: What this change of heart is about, I couldn't guess...

dialogues.speaker: Armand
dialogues.text: It's very s—s—simple and f—fun... D—Do you want to try?

response.speaker: Armand
response.text: I h—h—hope you... enjoy yourselves.

response.speaker: Armand
response.text: O—Okay! Y—You can come back any time... I'll b—be here.
